# Exercise: create your course folders

Time to use the terminal for real. In this exercise you create the folders that you will use for the rest of the course.

## The exercise

Do all of this **from the terminal**. Do not use Finder (Mac) or Explorer (Win).

1. Create a folder called `Programming` in your home directory.
2. Move into `Programming` and create a folder called `MCS` inside it.
3. Move into `MCS` and create six folders inside it: `module1`, `module2`, `module3`, `module4`, `module5` and `module6`.

> **Pro-tip.** Instead of your home directory, you can put `Programming` inside a folder that is automatically backed up, such as `Dropbox`, `OneDrive` or `Nextcloud`. Then your work survives a broken laptop.

## Check the result

When you are done, you should have this structure:

~~~text
home/
└── Programming/
    └── MCS/
        ├── module1/
        ├── module2/
        ├── module3/
        ├── module4/
        ├── module5/
        └── module6/
~~~

Now check if in Finder (Mac) or Explorer (Win) if you can locate these folders.

> On Linux, open your file manager (Files, Dolphin, Nautilus) and go to your home directory.

## Have it checked

Show your folder structure to a teacher or teaching assistant before you continue.
